name: librtlsdr
desc: Use Realtek DVB-T dongles as a cheap SDR
why: Turns a cheap DVB-T dongle into an SDR, the gateway to decoding the radio world around you.

brief.what_it_is: librtlsdr, the rtl-sdr project, is software for turning a Realtek RTL2832-based DVB-T USB dongle into a software-defined radio receiver. The README is one line long: it turns your Realtek RTL2832 based DVB dongle into a SDR receiver. The Homebrew formula lists eight executables: rtl_adsb, rtl_biast, rtl_eeprom, rtl_fm, rtl_power, rtl_sdr, rtl_tcp and rtl_test. I could not read the project's wiki, so I cannot confirm what each one does beyond their names.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no framing of its own beyond the one-line description. The scout note calls it a cheap way in to decoding the radio world around you, which is an editorial summary, not the author's words.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install was visible. The README has no build or setup steps, and the wiki that would hold them was blocked to me.
brief.standout: The hardware is a cheap TV-tuner dongle built for DVB-T broadcast, repurposed as a general radio receiver. The Homebrew formula bundles a set of command-line tools rather than a single program.
brief.status: unknown. The GitHub README shows no release date, version, or last-commit date, and I did not see the commit history.
brief.caveats: The official homepage, osmocom.org/projects/rtl-sdr/wiki, is behind an Anubis proof-of-work challenge that needs JavaScript and was not readable to me, so the main documentation is unread. The GitHub README is a single line that points to that wiki. The Homebrew formula gave no caveats.
quotes: turns your Realtek RTL2832 based DVB dongle into a SDR receiver
